title: Role-based access control (RBAC)
description: Permissions are granted to roles, and identities are assigned roles, instead of wiring permissions to individuals. An identity's effective permissions are the union of its roles' permissions. RBAC keeps permission management tractable as the number of identities grows. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers granting permissions via roles.

title: Attribute-based access control (ABAC)
description: ABAC evaluates policy rules over attributes of the subject, the resource, the action, and the environment. A rule like 'analysts may read datasets labeled internal during business hours' is evaluated per request. ABAC handles fine-grained cases RBAC cannot express. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers evaluating rules over subject/resource/action attributes.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"role": "analyst", "label": "internal", "hour": 10}, 2: {"role": "analyst", "label": "secret", "hour": 10}, 3: {"role": "analyst", "label": "internal", "hour": 23}}
a = CFG[LEVEL]
rule_ok = a["role"] == "analyst" and a["label"] in ("public", "internal") and 8 <= a["hour"] <= 18
print("request:", a, "| allowed:", rule_ok)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Least-privilege scope tokens
description: Tools receive short-lived tokens carrying only the scopes they need for the current task. A token for reading cannot write; a token for one database cannot touch another. Narrow scopes plus short lifetimes shrink the blast radius of a compromised token. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers issuing tokens with minimal scopes.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

t: Policy decision point / enforcement point split
title: Policy decision point / enforcement point split
description: The policy decision point (PDP) evaluates policy and returns a decision; the policy enforcement point (PEP) carries it out and cannot override it. Separating decision from enforcement lets one audited PDP serve many PEPs and keeps enforcement dumb and predictable. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers a PDP that only decides.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Permission caching with invalidation
description: Permission decisions are cached for speed, but the cache is invalidated the moment policy changes. A version counter on the policy lets cached entries detect staleness without a central invalidation bus. This gives fast checks with correct revocation. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers caching decisions keyed by subject/action/resource.
